headline: US Airlines Prioritize Fare Discipline Over Seat Capacity Amid Elevated Fuel Costs
summary: US passenger airlines are opting to fly with empty seats rather than discounting tickets, utilizing disciplined capacity management and higher fares to protect profitability against elevated jet fuel expenses.
why: Fuel represents one of the largest operating expenses for commercial airlines, and pricing power determines carriers' ability to defend operating margins.

impacts.name: Airlines
impacts.why: Disciplined pricing preserves unit revenues but limits passenger load factors amid higher jet fuel expenses.
